job_description_info.job_description:
# Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity

**Company:** Corvale Mobility (fictional name; intercity rail and coach operator)
**Location:** Kraków, Poland (contract, remote-friendly; occasional office days)
**Engagement:** Service agreement (B2B / freelance), not an employment contract
**Rate:** 95 – 125 PLN per hour

## The engagement

Corvale is preparing a new generation of trains and needs a cloud infrastructure engineer for the team that links the vehicles to the company's cloud platform. You will help shape the architecture from the start and take it to production.

## Scope

- Design, build and operate the cloud infrastructure that links on-board train systems with backend services: telemetry ingestion, alerting, video streaming and remote content updates
- Maintain the infrastructure-as-code repository (Terraform with Terragrunt), keeping it tidy and approachable
- Lead technical proposals across backend and infrastructure from idea to production
- Contribute to system design and challenge decisions with arguments
- Set up secure train-to-cloud communication (mutual TLS, certificate management, network design)
- Agree interfaces and responsibilities with train manufacturers' engineers
- Support backend developers in deploying services that are easy to monitor and run
- Keep the platform observable, reliable and secure

## Requirements

- Hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud environment design and operation
- AWS preferred; other major clouds acceptable
- Strong Terraform and Terragrunt
- Good understanding of systems architecture and system design
- Networking knowledge, including mTLS and SSL/TLS
- Practical security awareness
- Experience leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along
- Strong analytical thinking and clear communication

**Nice to have:** IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, backend or full-stack background (JVM preferred), Linux and virtual machines.

## Working model

Independent contractor, invoicing monthly for agreed services.

company_info.company_description:
Corvale Mobility is a privately held, Kraków-based transportation and software company providing long-distance bus and passenger-rail travel across Central Europe. Its online platform supports booking, trip tracking and travel extras. The company uses an asset-light model, working with regional operators on many routes while managing its brand, booking technology and network planning. It is expanding its rail service and prioritizing greater use of data and machine learning.

Corvale describes itself as engineering-led and technology-first, with teams that take end-to-end ownership of their systems. Its stated values are “Lead, Shape, Own, Enjoy the journey,” alongside sustainability, shared goals and collaborative problem-solving. Employees have described the culture as collaborative, fast-moving and open to new ideas; the company highlights professional development, appreciation, work-life flexibility and employee feedback. It also offers international teams, hybrid work in many employee roles, career ownership and travel benefits on its network.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role focused on Fleet Connectivity. I bring hands-on experience operating cloud infrastructure, building Terraform-based networking, and automating application releases. The opportunity to help shape infrastructure for a new train-to-cloud platform particularly appeals to me because it combines cloud design, networking, security, and dependable operations.

At Havenstad Logistics, I work in a three-person cloud team operating an Azure estate of approximately 400 virtual machines and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions. I have developed Terraform modules for hub-and-spoke networking, Azure Firewall, and private endpoints, and migrated release pipelines for 15 internal applications to Azure DevOps YAML. Earlier, as a Systems Administrator, I led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS and automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.

This experience has given me a practical foundation in cloud infrastructure, systems administration, networking, and security. In freelance work, I also established backups and basic security baselines—including MFA and conditional access—for small businesses. I would bring that combination of infrastructure engineering and operational focus to Corvale’s work on secure, observable, and reliable fleet connectivity, while contributing to the collaborative, end-to-end ownership described in the role.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience with Azure, Terraform, cloud networking, and release automation could support Corvale Mobility’s fleet connectivity platform. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
